messages.text: I set aside your little jars from Sunday. Do you still want them for the windowsill starts?
Yes, please. I am trying peppers first and maybe one tray of tomatoes if the light cooperates.
Good. I also have ginger and honey if your throat still feels scratchy after work.
I will grab both when I stop by. I am making broth tonight with the smoked turkey piece from Sunday.
Did you see Sister Evelyn's post about Saturday's pantry shift? She put the sign-up under the church page again.
I saw it after Aunt Rochelle tagged me in the cousin photos. I marked us for 10:00 and then closed the app before that county budget post pulled me in.
Good. Please send me the real article on that budget thing when you find it. People are sharing half a sentence like that is the whole story.
Already looking for the Cleveland.com piece. I am giving myself until dinner is done, then the phone goes face down.
I put three holds on mystery options at Lakewood. You are not allowed to blame me when one keeps you up past midnight.
Too late, I already saw the cover with the old theater and added it to my list.
Naturally. Also, if Sunday opens up after church, Keisha said she can do Toast at 12:30 before the Cavs game.
That works. I will bring the hot sauce she asked about and the book notes you bullied me into making.
Tasha is held up at the clinic and I am stuck with a boiler issue. Any chance you can grab Maya from Jefferson at 4:20?
I can do 4:20. Tell her I will be in the blue coat by the side door, then I will bring her to your place.
Appreciate it. Mom said she still wants you at dinner Sunday, so don't let this turn into you skipping.
Denise already texted me about cornbread, so I know I am accounted for.
Tasha asked what to put next to our name for Sunday. Greens or mac?
Put greens for y'all. I already started the sheet, and Mama said Aunt Cheryl is bringing mac.
Cool. Also don't act brand new when Jr. asks for one of those corner biscuits.
He can have one if he gets there before they disappear into foil packs.
Saw them blue lights all along Brookwood this morning. Remember what I told you.
I do. Window down, both hands where they can see them, no reaching for my wallet until they ask.
Good. And that city meeting tonight has the stop numbers on the agenda, right?
Yes. I printed the agenda with the complaint dashboard and the clinic van item marked.
Your mama says the fellowship hall signup is missing your greens and that pie. I told her you were probably in spreadsheets.
Tell her I already bought the sweet potatoes. I am bringing greens too, but I need your big pot back.
Big pot is clean. Pastor Greene asked if you can look over that young man's resume after the 11 o'clock.
Yes, I can give him 20 minutes before dinner. I still owe Mrs. Ellis the opening reading, so keep me moving.
You made it to the 6:30 class after that day? I would have gone straight home and stared at the wall.
Barely made it, but I needed the music loud and somebody else counting. My shoulders finally dropped by the third song.
That tracks. Please eat something real before you open that laptop again.
Heating leftovers now. Shoes are already by the door for tomorrow morning, so I am not negotiating with myself at 5:50.
Did your 9 o'clock meeting go all right? I prayed you remembered to slow down and let them hear every word.
I did. I kept my voice even when Brad tried to rush past the budget gap.
Good. You know how rooms like that can hear a little firmness as something else. Facts first, calm face, paper trail.
Exactly. I sent the recap before I left the parking garage.
You still at the office, or did that new intake screen finally behave?
Leaving now. I had to compare the old spreadsheet numbers against what the new queue said before Monday.
That sounds like a Friday crime. Did your chart at least prove where the slowdown is?
Mostly. The handoff column is ugly, so I dropped a note in the channel and scheduled a quick screen-share.
Are we still doing Lakewood brunch tomorrow, or did your Tuesday/Thursday desk calendar eat the week again?
Brunch is safe. I only moved tonight's chapter review because the mock quiz opened early.
Respectfully, your color-coded blocks are terrifying. Bring the book list and leave the spreadsheet energy at home.
No promises. The same spreadsheet is keeping my exam hours, process notes, and next-step role postings from becoming soup.
Can you be backup for Jayden's pickup next Thursday if Tasha gets held late?
I can, but text me by Wednesday night. I already have that Thursday box in the sheet marked for gas, groceries, and the school fundraiser.
You and those boxes. I just need the kid collected, CPA Johnson.
Laugh all you want. Last month landed at 4,300 because three small 'it's fine' items became one loud number.
I left Zumba early and sat in the parking lot making a list on the back of the receipt. Rollout fixes, Mom's portal message, PMP chapters, Sunday food.
Voice note coming. Also: you do not have to solve Cleveland by midnight, ma'am.
Please send it. My head keeps replaying every loose end like I missed the one thing that will make tomorrow messy.
Start with shower, water, and one page in that notebook. We can talk after church if it is still loud in there.
I found the Savannah walking tour with the church stops and the old square route. It is 90 minutes, which sounds kinder than the three-hour one.
The Savannah food tour emailed me again. Should I keep the link or let it go?
I found two copies of the new mystery at the Lakewood branch. Want me to hold one for Thursday?
Send it. I am trying to keep one thing on the calendar each day, then leave room for lunch, shade, and sitting somewhere pretty.
Keep it, please. I slid that whole little weekend idea into early summer.
Yes please. I need to dig last month's pages out from under the green score folder on my desk.
Early summer works. Also, I found that green wrap dress you liked marked down.
Very Miranda. Also the Gullah cooking class has a $40 deposit, and the April seats were already half gone.
Do not tempt me. That tab is staying parked until the patio chair stops staring at me from the statement.
That desk sounds like an archaeological site with better snacks.
I can do the deposit after this paycheck. I still have the Chicago hotel alert open too, so I am pacing myself.
Accurate. If I can clear one corner after the 8:00 run, I can bring both books and those extra pages.
Mom handed me that envelope from the clinic. Looks like numbers and codes, not a real sentence.
Bring it Sunday. I want to compare the $35 desk charge against the card portal before anyone pays twice.
You and those portals. Also, did your job finally post the new holiday list? Tasha is trying to pick a cookout date.
Yes, Memorial Day is locked and my vacation hours reset in the same system. I'll check after I upload Mom's paper.
Mom said you already handled that insurance letter. You want me to cover the takeout Sunday?
I can do dessert, but takeout would help. The house draft and Honda pull both hit before payday.
Say less. I got it. Your spreadsheet probably has Sunday dinner in cell B47 anyway.
B48, actually. I am waiting for the miles account to close before I send the full amount.
You still want me to swing by and look at that loose railing before Sunday dinner?
Yes please. I have the bracket and anchors in the garage, just need your toolbox brain.
Coffee first, railing second. Also keep those repair receipts with the house papers.
Already in the blue folder with the Strongsville closing stuff. I learned from Denise's spreadsheets.
You sounded steady on the second verse this morning. I saw you breathe before that high part.
I almost came in early on the new ending, but Angela caught my eye from the front row.
That is why practice matters. Are you still coming by for dinner after you change out of the robe?
Yes. Give me 30 minutes. That last song settled my whole morning down.
Brunch was cute, but I forgot to ask: did that garage invoice ever come through?
Yes, $407. I moved it from the separate Ally bucket and left the electric and mortgage drafts alone.
Look at you making the spreadsheet behave. I would have stared at it, sighed, and ordered fries.
I still ordered fries. But I also changed the next transfer from $275 to $325 for the 15th.
The library forum added a panel on ballot access and school funding. You still want me to save two seats?
Yes. I want the part with actual numbers, not just applause lines.
Very on brand. I also saw the clinic expansion question is on the handout.
Good. I can handle a long evening if they talk about how any of it gets carried out.
I found the library link for the Lakewood forum. The judge panel starts at 6:15, then council questions after.
Send it. I already have two tabs open and a little table started, because apparently that is who I am on a Sunday.
Adding the plain-language guide too. It is dry, but at least it puts everyone on one page.
Perfect. I will compare that with the local write-up before book club.
Ma asked if you can look at that portal letter tonight. You still at the office?
Just got home. I stayed late to clean up the Friday numbers and move two piles around before Monday.
You and those spreadsheets. Didn't they give you that corner desk around the time Jayden started kindergarten?
Pretty much. Five Marches of people stopping by it with problems they could have emailed.
Your mother says that MetroHealth thing sent another code to her phone. We are at the table whenever you get here.
Save the text and don't close the screen. I'll look after we eat, before Marcus tries to make everybody watch highlights.
Found that old shoebox in the hall closet. Some of your granddad's papers say Meridian on them.
Please set those aside. I want to copy a few for the June table at church.
Fine. I also set aside that envelope from Anthem. Looks like it wants numbers from the last visit.
Bring both to the dining room. I can scan the envelope and send the office question before I head home.
I put them with the Birmingham photo. Your mother said do not let me tape anything, so I am obeying orders.
Good. No tape on the old paper, Dad. I will bring sleeves after dinner.
You still need that folding table from my garage for Tuesday night?
Yes please. The resume station keeps turning into a paper avalanche without it.
I'll put it by the back door. Same place you had those gym cones last week.
Perfect. I'll grab it after dinner and return both before Mom starts counting what's missing.
Your mama said you were bringing something after church. Need me to pull the cooler from the garage?
Yes please. I have grilled chicken cooling and a pan of vegetables that need to ride flat.
Cooler is by the back door. I also found two freezer packs that still have some life in them.
Perfect. I am trying to make these stretch through Thursday and not buy lunch near work.
You made it back from your parents' okay last night? You went quiet after the pie picture.
Yeah. Got home, put the containers away, and the place felt extra still. I let the phone sit instead of checking every new favor text.
Good. A phone on silent is not a character flaw. Eat the leftovers and call me after Zumba if you want.
Deal. I already portioned one serving for tomorrow and left the rest in the freezer.
Your mama says you left that little cuff by the chair again. You checking yours or mine this time?
Both if you sit still long enough. I wrote my 126 over 78 in the phone log this morning.
I will sit if you bring coffee. Also Denise asked if you saw that new March page from the state site.
I saw it. I am sending her Dr. Patel's message too so she stops forwarding every cousin's screenshot.
Did you make it back from that park Saturday without overdoing it?
Yes, I kept it to the Ledges loop and did my step-downs before I left the house.
Good. Wear the newer shoes if you go again. You know how you get when the weather first turns nice.
I know. Saturday was easy pace, then rest Sunday after dinner.
I put the Slaughter title on hold for you. Also, Thursday's room is only ours until 7:20, so we may need efficient opinions.
Efficient opinions from this group? Bold. I can bring the hummus tray and my notes if we are doing the quick version.
Quick version, then over to Keisha's before the first quarter gets away from us.
Perfect. I will park by Detroit Ave so I can make the handoff without circling for twenty minutes.
Found that old photo box in the basement. Your mother saved everything from the Cleveland hospital packet.
Of course she did. Please keep the envelope with the 1986 papers out of the coffee zone.
I know where to put paper. Same folder has Marcus grinning by the Parma mailbox.
That mailbox picture is going to make him deny everything at dinner.
Can you call me before you get settled tonight? I only have two portal questions.
Yes, before 6:10 works. After that I am putting the pan on, giving the windowsill plants a soak, and closing the laptop.
That is fine. Eat something warm and do not sit there with the lights on until all hours.
I will try. This last stack of pages has been pulling me back in after the dishes.
Baby, did your 4 o'clock screen practice go all right? You sounded worn out yesterday.
It ran long. I'm still cooking, so call me in ten and I'll put you on speaker.
I will. Also Dr. Huang's nurse replied, but the button says view summary and then spins.
Leave it alone for now. When we talk, read me the first line and I'll tell you if it needs a reply tonight.
Maya said the shoebox city needs glue sticks, gray paper, and something for tiny windows by Friday.
I have glue sticks here. I can stop at Target tomorrow for the paper and a cheap pack of clear labels.
Good. Marcus and Tasha are juggling enough this week, and Robert already promised Jayden he would check the loose bike chain.
Then I will drop supplies after work and stay long enough to cut windows straight.
You still coming over Saturday or did the purple sneakers take you out again? 😂
Saturday is safe. I just have to wash the pans Friday night and move the orange cones off the printer chair.
Only you would have dinner prep, printer drama, and tiny practice cones in the same sentence.
That room is doing a lot this month. I will bring the lemon chicken and not the cones.
That reel you sent with the kettlebell circuit was cute, but please tell me you did not keep reading the comments under that city schools post.
Nope. I saved the workout, checked WKSU for the school story, and shut it down when the timer buzzed.
I listened to your voice note. You did not owe them ten extra apologies for asking for the sign-off you already earned.
Progress. A timer and a reputable link, look at you acting grown on a Thursday night.
I know. Old habit. I caught myself and changed the last sentence before sending it.
That part. Polished does not mean shrinking. Also that copper blouse in the photo? Meeting armor.
Do not start. I still have tomorrow's ops article sitting in LinkedIn saved items, but that can wait until coffee.
Ha. Keeping it for Monday's steering group then.
For book club, are you assigning food again or should I bring whatever survives my workday?
I made a little list. You can do salad or cups. I have the oven stuff covered.
Your 'little list' usually has tabs. I respect the commitment.
Tabs prevent three bags of ice and no plates. Also I saved two biscuits from Sunday if you want one with coffee.
Art festival opens at 6:00 Thursday. Does your east-side music thing run late again?
If Ms. Angela keeps the tenors on that bridge, yes. I can meet you closer to 8:15.
Then I will browse slowly and pretend I am making scholarly choices about pottery.
Please do. I need the run-through first. It untangles my brain better than going straight from spreadsheets to crowds.
Tasha may get stuck at work Friday. Can you be backup for Jalen pickup at 5:30?
Only if both of you are truly stuck. I already moved two work calls, Dad's bill review, and my study block around this week.
Fair. Emergency only. I can take Dad's bill if you send the login steps.
Thank you. I wrote the steps down so I stop running tomorrow in my head before it gets here.
Dominion letter came to Mom's by mistake. Your name, Strongsville address.
Thanks. Toss it in your car and I'll grab it Sunday. Gas bill is due next Friday anyway.
Want me to open it and read the damage?
No, I already budgeted March utilities after the FirstKey draft. Just need the paper copy.
Your mother says ask you before I pay this knee visit thing. I was going to just mail the check.
Please don't mail it yet. If the office only posts a $25 copay, the rest may adjust after the claim finishes.
Fine. I will put the checkbook back before I hurt somebody's accounting.
Thank you. I am doing my own eye appointment estimate tonight too, so all these little numbers are in one spreadsheet.
Your mother says don't let that online class run through dinner. Chicken will be done at 6:45.
I set the timer for 7:00-8:00 after dishes. Tonight is charts, handoffs, and why people skip steps when the form is annoying.
That sounds like every plant meeting I ever survived.
Exactly. That class at work is still the reason I stopped just complaining about bottlenecks and filled out the opening packet.
Good morning. Please send me the June 19 program draft when you get a chance. The youth table still needs two volunteers.
I will send it before my 9:00 call. I can also ask the operations interns if they want to sit at the career table.
That would help. Also, remember to add Mrs. Tate's family to the list for Sunday morning.
Already wrote them down. I will bring the printed list and the red drink recipe card.
Your Aunt Carol called. She found another envelope from your cousin's old case and is worried there is still a balance.
Tell her not to pay anything today. I will look at the dates and fees after work.
Thank you. That season wore everybody down, and half of it was just standing in lines and finding money.
Exactly why I wrote a note for Monday's session about fines, ride vouchers, and plain-language notices.
You still looking at that April porch-and-fried-fish situation, or did real life snatch the envelope?
Envelope survived. I put $60 in after groceries, and I am skipping the random Target aisle this week.
Good. You need a bench under trees, a plate someone else cooked, and zero spreadsheets for at least two afternoons.
That is the exact image keeping me from clicking buy on every cute shoe I see.
Did your office lunch get spicy after you brought those promotion charts?
A little. I kept it to the data, the mentoring budget, and who gets tapped for stretch projects.
That sounds like you: receipts first, sermon second.
I also sent the youth center receipt before I forgot. March made me remember to stop just talking.
For book club dinner, are you doing the greens with the smoked turkey again or should I bring something that does not compete?
Bring the bread. I found good greens and a parsley bundle last weekend, so I am keeping the pot simple.
Excellent. Also, the library plant swap flyer says tomato and basil starts go fast. Naturally, people are competitive about tiny leaves.
Send it to me. If mine stay alive until April, I will still look for one basil backup.
That patio chair receipt come through yet? Your mother said it was not cheap.
It came through. I already moved a couple of fun tabs out of March.
Good. Furniture that keeps folks off the floor comes before hotel pillows.
And before my pretty work outfits, apparently.
Good morning. Did your pharmacy clinic put the sticker on your card, or do you need me to scan the old one?
Before I go to Aldi, do you need oatmeal or eggs? They have both marked down this morning.
Happy 40th, sweetheart. I put the sweet-potato pie in the oven early so it will be set before everyone comes.
They added it. I took a picture and put it with the MyChart files.
Eggs, please. I have peppers left, so I can bake another tray of cups for the mornings.
Thank you, Mom. Please do not let Daddy start retelling the snow-in-Cleveland story before I get there.
Thank you. I read three different posts and closed them. I will wait for what Dr. Patel sends.
I will pick them up. Also check your cabinet before you buy beans again; you had two bags last Sunday.
Your father has already practiced it. Marcus said he is bringing the kids after their game.
You are right. I am using those with the frozen greens instead of adding more to the cart.
That is the better plan. I checked Cleveland Clinic's page too, and it matches what his office said.
Then I am bringing extra patience and a knife for the pie.
Your school board spreadsheet came up at brunch and I need you to know I laughed with love.
It is not a spreadsheet, it is three columns and one color code. Very restrained.
Uh huh. Did you at least add what the counselor group said about the levy language?
Yes. I put that next to the Sun News piece and the district page so I can sort it out later.
Lauren just sent me the screenshot of that print booth near Gordon Square. The one with the bright yellow windows is very you.
I saved it last night. The artist posted a little process reel and now I want to see the whole table in person.
Then we go after Zumba. I need food first though, because nobody deserves my personality on an empty stomach 😂
Deal. Texting Lauren now so she can pick the route with the least chaotic parking.
Malik said your squad was running suicides like it was the NBA combine.
Tell him he noticed the one hard part and missed the twenty minutes of footwork.
Mom says you need the big folding board from my garage for that June thing.
Yes, the one from the kids' science fair. I am mapping the Alabama side on the left and Mississippi on the right.
He also said you made them shake hands with the little kids after. Very Miranda.
If they can talk trash during warmups, they can learn eye contact after.
Cool. I will drop it Sunday. Do not make me spell Attalla in marker.
I have labels printed already. You only have to carry the board and act useful.
Can you be backup Tuesday at 3:20 if Maya's rehearsal runs over? Tasha and I may both get stuck.
I can be the emergency option, but I can't take the regular slot this week. Work deck, PMP chapter, and I blocked my Tuesday evening.
Fair. Emergency only. I know you still have to get back across town and do your whole quiet-house decompression thing.
Exactly. If you confirm by noon Tuesday, I can adjust. Otherwise I'm keeping the block.
You still heading to Keisha's tonight or did Lauren's stack of pages wear everybody out?
Still going. I read the last chapter during lunch, so nobody can accuse me of freeloading on snacks.
Tell them if Darius starts cold, my son says switch seats by halftime. Scientific method.
Noted. I am not promising your nephew's couch superstition gets peer review.
Your mother says you are going down near Peninsula again. Trail dry enough?
Mostly. I am staying on Towpath if the rocks are slick, and I put the blue inserts back in.
Smart. Coffee can fix many things, but not bad footing.
Exactly. Short drive, careful start, brunch after.
You still coming by for Cavs snacks or did the Monday crew trap you again?
Give me 30. I had to walk Darnell through the new form, check Tia's totals, and call back that angry caller from 4:20.
That sounds like three separate people borrowing your nervous system. Bring chips, not a case file.
Chips are already in the car. I am trying to keep this week under 45 before Friday laughs at me.
Voice note when you can. That class clearly did not shake off whatever was sitting on your shoulders.
It was the new workflow blowing up all day, then Mom's numbers visit got moved and the office message wouldn't open right.
No wonder. Eat something and do not turn into tech support at 10 p.m. unless Denise truly needs you.
I told her I'd call after my shower, just to make sure she heard the nurse correctly.
The art museum tickets are cheaper if we grab them tonight. Are you still in for Saturday?
I found the next pick at Lakewood. Do you want me to hold it, or are you still finishing the one with the cracked green spine?
Yes. Use the travel one and I will send you my half after the full-statement draw clears in the morning.
Hold it for me, please. I am stirring soup and trying not to scorch garlic between chapters.
That is the most organized sentence anyone has ever sent about museum tickets.
That sounds very you. Please water the basil before it files a complaint.
Already done. If I stop at 25 pages tonight, I may actually sleep before midnight.
I have to keep it clean this week. Aidvantage extra went out, and Honda is due before book club.
Your mama says that insurance letter is nonsense. Want me to bring it Sunday?
Bring it. I have a folder for her portal stuff, your knee bill, and the running notes.
Running notes sounds serious for two old folks and one envelope.
It keeps surprise envelopes from eating the whole month. March is tracking toward 3,800 if nothing else jumps out.
Are you still coming by after work, or did that office changeover keep you late again?
I can still come. I just need ten minutes to answer the Outlook thread and update the tracker from today's test forms.
Eat something before you start fixing everybody's forms. Bring the insurance letter and I will put on tea.
I sent you the West Side Market pasta pop-up from the restaurant account. Also, the library board rumor floating around looks suspiciously trimmed.
Saved the pasta post. For the board thing, I found the meeting packet instead of trusting the screenshot.
A librarian approves. Are you still doing your lunch-hour-only rule for scrolling?
Yes. After 1:00 I am back to the workflow deck, and the art fair account can tempt me later.
Library has two seats left for the forum Tuesday. Agenda says stop data, complaint outcomes, and budget shifts.
Hold me one. I want to ask how residents can see patterns without filing three records requests.
Very librarian of you. Also, do you want the handout on record-sealing clinics?
Yes. My aunt still gets nervous every time paperwork shows up with my cousin's name on it.
Mom wants the old Parma picture for the frame, the one from when you were 16 and I had that terrible Cavs jacket.
That jacket was loud enough to need its own room.
Dad says do not crop out his garage shelves. Man is still proud of that setup.
I will scan it as-is. Mom, Dad, shelves, jacket, all of it.
The library has a planning room open Wednesday at 6. Want me to hold it for your June 19 committee packet review?
Please hold it. I need space for the vendor list, the recipe cards, and the mock-interview signup sheet.
Done. I also found a local oral-history display that might pair well with the program.
Perfect. I can stop by after midweek study and bring the packet edits.
You still taking the kids through drills at 10 or did the rain cancel you?
Gym backup. Ten little layup experts and one auntie with a whistle.
My son better not come home talking like he invented defense.
No promises. I am walking the long way around the block first so I show up with patience.
Dad said he has two spare stakes in the garage. You still need them or are the tomato cages enough?
I will take the stakes. The peppers can use them later, and I need to patch the bed before it gets warm.
Cool. I am passing that Lorain Ave stand after Jamal's practice. Want anything if they have the early greens?
Yes, one bag if it looks fresh. I can pay you back Sunday.
Jayden left that blue mouthguard on my workbench. You passing the rec center before tipoff?
Yes. I will swing by your garage at 9:10 and take it over with the granola bars.
Good. Denise says Marcus forgot the snack bag again. That boy plans like a busted tape measure.
I will cover snacks. Tell Denise I heard her about not buying the neon sugar drinks.
Your mama says the list is missing drinks. I can grab two cases after I get gas.
Please do. I moved rolls to Aunt Cheryl and put you down for drinks.
Good. Need anything for that orange pie you keep making, or is the kitchen laboratory stocked?
Stocked except foil. If you see the deep tins, grab one pack.
I packed greens and two slices of pie for you. Do not forget them on the counter this time.
Thank you. I'll take one slice for tonight and freeze the other before I sit down.
And when you get home, leave Robert's insurance letter until tomorrow. It can wait one night.
I hear you. I wrote Monday 6:30 on the envelope and I'm not opening the portal tonight.
Did you look at that escrow letter? Do not let them sneak a change past you.
I checked it after dinner. It bumps the payment $28 in May, so I adjusted the sheet and kept the six-month column where it was.
Good. Know the numbers first, then decide. That is how you stay ready.
Exactly. March still shows 4.2 after the garage charge clears.
Did you eat the keys-day cupcake or just stare at it like a Hallmark movie? 😂
Ate it proudly. I was thinking about that tiny closing room and all those pay stubs in my folder.
I remember you bringing spreadsheets to brunch like they were sacred texts.
They still run the place. Roof line, utilities, FirstKey, emergency fund. Unromantic but peaceful.
Are you stopping by after the pantry shift, or should I save your plate for tomorrow?
Save it for tomorrow, please. I need to change clothes, print the roster, and find the alto pages before 7:15.
Please put things in one bag before you leave. Last time you were searching three piles and talking about being on time.
I know. The printer tray, jersey bag, and music folder are already on the little table by the door.
Please tell me you ate something between the gym and those packet reviews.
Did you ever book the dentist before your March money bucket disappears? I remembered because my crown quote almost made me leave my body.
Half a granola bar in the car, which does not count, I know.
Booked for April 9. I am using the pretax card for the cleaning part and keeping the bigger estimate in next month's budget.
It absolutely does not. Also Dana texted me that your salary-band sheet saved her from underselling herself.
Good. Now I just need tomorrow's eighth-graders to stop traveling before I lose my voice.
Responsible adult content. Meanwhile I used my personal day to sit on the couch and watch old sitcoms.
Honestly deserved. I checked my own time bank today and saved one day for Mom's follow-up just in case.
For Saturday: Rocky River reservation at 9:15, then coffee? I checked, the trail by the nature center is not a mud soup situation.
Perfect. I have lakefront miles Thursday morning and class that evening, so Saturday can be hills without me pretending to be heroic.
Noted. I will bring snacks and avoid choosing the route that feels like a character-building subplot.
Mom said you got her asking me who is on my ballot now. What did you start?
I gave her the plain-language sheet. Judges, schools, clinic money, and who actually has a plan.
As long as it is shorter than your work emails.
Two pages. And I left room for the legal fund receipt so she can stop asking whether I mailed it.
Mom said your work thing went smoother today. Nobody broke the new buttons?
Only one routing mistake. I showed them the Power BI page with yesterday vs today and folks finally stopped arguing from memory.
So the scoreboard won. Same thing I tell my crew when they swear the pump was checked.
Exactly. Tomorrow I clean up the Excel export and pin the quick notes in Teams.
Did you still want me to look at that blue suit jacket after my appointment tomorrow?
Thank you, but let it sit. I am keeping March plain until the chair and card clear.
That is sensible. We can also wait on talking through the hotel choices until after Easter dinner.
Yes, let's do that. I still want the weekend, just not on this month's pile.
Did you eat before starting my insurance letter? It can wait until Saturday morning.
I ate. I caught myself opening the portal, the work tracker, and my study notes all at once, so I closed two tabs.
Good. Handle one paper at a time. Say your morning prayer again if you need to reset.
I walked around the block and put the letter on tomorrow's list. I am keeping tonight small.
I found the lost wine-gold beads from last time. They were in my mixing bowl, which feels like our brand.
That tracks. I still have Lauren's paperback in my tote next to the tortilla chips.
Bring both tonight. We can do chapter drama first, then yell at the refs like civilized adults.
I will be there by 6:40. Saving my loudest objections for the third quarter.
You made it to the Thursday run-through after that meeting marathon?
Barely. But once we got into the old call-and-response piece, my shoulders finally dropped.
Good. Because your calendar has been doing the absolute most.
I know. I still want Sunday morning covered, though. The new arrangement needs one more clean pass.
Can you look at Dad's insurance letter tomorrow, or are you doing your Thursday school-night thing?
